bio: Timothy R. Smith is Director of the Computational Neuroscience Outcomes Center (CNOC) in the Department of Neurosurgery at Brigham and Women's Hospital and an Associate Professor of Neurosurgery at Harvard Medical School. Trained additionally as an epidemiologist and statistician, he is best known as a data-science / outcomes-research neurosurgeon-scientist applying epidemiology, biostatistics, and machine learning to neurosurgical outcomes. Clinically he treats brain and spine tumors — gliomas, meningiomas, and metastatic disease — but his primary academic identity is predictive analytics rather than high-volume ablative surgery.

bio: William T. Curry is a national leader in the neurosurgical care of brain, skull-base, and spine tumors and in translational brain-tumor immunology at Massachusetts General Hospital. He has been on the MGH neurosurgical faculty since 2004, directs Neurosurgical Oncology, was co-director of Mass General Neuroscience, and in February 2025 became Mass General Brigham's Chief Medical Officer for academic medical centers. Clinically he manages benign and malignant tumors using both open and endoscopic/minimally invasive techniques; his research centers on immunotherapy and cellular (CAR-T) approaches for malignant gliomas. His growing administrative role has reduced personal operative volume.
